lead.headline: WPI hits a series high as MoRTH sets a 2029 BS-VII date; BHEL profit doubles
lead.dek: September wholesale inflation rose to 11.39%, and brokers expect commodity costs to compress Q2 auto margins even as revenue grows by up to 28%. A draft BS-VII deadline of April 2029 surprised carmakers, while BHEL's Q2 and fresh T&D wins point to a firm capex cycle.

ticker.text: WPI inflation rises to a series-high 11.39% in September; fuel & power at 25.85%
MoRTH draft sets BS-VII norms for cars and SUVs from 1 April 2029; industry prefers 2032
BHEL Q2FY27 consolidated profit up 119% to ₹820.94 cr; revenue up 24% to ₹9,300 cr
Kalpataru Projects wins ~₹2,225 cr of orders; FY27 YTD inflows ~₹20,000 cr
Brokers see Q2 auto revenue up 26–28% YoY, with copper and rubber costs pressuring margins
CEAT Q2 revenue up 26% to ₹4,762 cr; net profit down 40% to ₹112 cr
Electric car retail tops 1.92 lakh units in H1 FY27, up 89% YoY; Tata holds 40% share
GreenCell Mobility raises ₹330 cr equity from Impact Fund Denmark for ~4,500 e-buses

Boeing delivers 161 commercial jets in Q3, taking 2026 YTD deliveries to 475

ev.headline: Electric car retail crosses 1.92 lakh units in H1 FY27, up 89% YoY
ev.summary: Vahan data compiled by Autocar Professional shows 1,92,012 electric passenger vehicles registered in April–September, up from 1,01,398 a year earlier. Q2 alone accounted for 1,04,009 units, up 84% YoY. Tata Motors leads with 76,745 units (40% share), followed by Mahindra (44,051; 23%) and JSW MG Motor (33,456; 17%), whose share has fallen from 29% a year ago.
ev.whyItMatters: Share is concentrating in the two domestic leaders while JSW MG's lead erodes, a shift that matters for valuation benchmarks and for any strategic or capital-raising discussions involving the smaller e-PV players.

ev.headline: GreenCell Mobility raises ₹330 crore from Impact Fund Denmark for e-bus rollout
ev.summary: The Eversource Capital-backed electric bus operator has secured ₹330 crore in equity from Impact Fund Denmark. The capital will fund execution of its existing order book of about 4,500 new e-buses, which would take its fleet past 5,000 buses across 105 cities. Existing investors include IFC, British International Investment and Tata Capital.
ev.whyItMatters: Development-finance and impact capital continues to anchor India's e-bus operating platforms, which are building scale ahead of potential consolidation or a listing.

ev.headline: Changan and CATL to add 25 GWh of joint battery capacity
ev.summary: Changan and CATL plan a new 5 billion yuan (about US$750 million) battery facility that will add 25 GWh within three years of starting operations in 2027, taking joint capacity to 75 GWh. The partners will also work on solid-state and sodium-ion cells; Changan targets 400 Wh/kg solid-state cells with commercial production in 2027.
ev.whyItMatters: Chinese OEM-cell maker tie-ups keep pushing down cell costs and raising the scale threshold that India's PLI-ACC entrants must meet.

autos.headline: Q2 auto revenue seen up as much as 28%, but input costs squeeze margins
autos.summary: Brokerage previews peg sector revenue growth at 26–28% YoY for Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up only 14–16% and PAT up 12–13%. Maruti Suzuki's revenue is seen rising 28–30% while its profit is estimated to fall 8–15%; TVS Motor stands out with expected PAT growth of 45–49%. Elara Securities notes copper up 6% and rubber up 9% QoQ.
autos.whyItMatters: Volume growth is not translating into proportional earnings, so margin assumptions, not unit forecasts, are likely to drive estimate revisions this season.

autos.headline: CEAT Q2: revenue up 26% but net profit falls 40% on raw-material costs
autos.summary: CEAT's consolidated revenue rose to ₹4,762 crore from ₹3,773 crore a year earlier, but EBITDA fell 9% to ₹457 crore and the margin narrowed to about 9.6% from 13.3%. Net profit dropped to ₹112 crore from ₹186 crore. Standalone revenue grew 23% to ₹4,548 crore.
autos.whyItMatters: A clear early read on commodity pressure across auto ancillaries; pricing power and pass-through terms will separate component names in Q2.

autos.headline: Average car loan size up 49% to ₹8.2 lakh in seven years: TransUnion CIBIL
autos.summary: The average passenger-vehicle loan rose to ₹8.2 lakh in H1 2026 from H1 2019, with a 62-month average tenure. Two-wheeler loan balances have grown 3.2 times to ₹1.76 trillion. PV loans more than 90 days overdue fell to 0.5% from 1.45%.
autos.whyItMatters: Larger tickets and better asset quality support premiumisation, but a rising-rate environment makes financing costs a sensitivity to watch in volume forecasts.

industrials.headline: BHEL Q2FY27 profit more than doubles; board approves Haridwar capacity capex
industrials.summary: Consolidated net profit rose 119% YoY to ₹820.94 crore and revenue from operations grew 24% to ₹9,300.35 crore. Power segment revenue was ₹6,637.90 crore and Industry ₹2,662.45 crore. H1 profit was ₹1,197.65 crore against a loss a year earlier, and the board approved about ₹500 crore of capex for additional thermal and nuclear manufacturing facilities at Haridwar.
industrials.whyItMatters: Execution on the thermal order book is now reaching the P&L, and fresh capacity capex signals management confidence in a multi-year power equipment cycle.

industrials.headline: Kalpataru Projects adds ~₹2,225 crore of orders; FY27 inflows up over 30%
industrials.summary: Kalpataru Projects International disclosed new orders and a letter of comfort worth about ₹2,225 crore, including roughly ₹2,031 crore of domestic and international T&D work. Its Swedish subsidiary won a ₹194 crore (SEK 200 million) substation contract from Ellevio. FY27 year-to-date inflows stand at about ₹20,000 crore, up more than 30% YoY.
industrials.whyItMatters: Continued T&D order momentum, including in Europe, reinforces the grid theme that is drawing strategic and sponsor interest across EPC, transformers and cables.

industrials.headline: NCLAT stays insolvency admission against Polycab over ₹2.79 crore dues
industrials.summary: NCLT Ahmedabad had admitted an operational-creditor petition by Asier Metals over alleged dues of ₹2.79 crore on 7 October; the NCLAT stayed that order on 9 October and listed the appeal for 26 October. Polycab says it is debt-free, with net cash above ₹4,000 crore and net worth of ₹11,682 crore, and expects no material impact.
industrials.whyItMatters: Largely a procedural matter for a cash-rich company, but it shows how small operational disputes can trigger IBC proceedings, which is relevant for diligence on supplier disputes.

aerospace-defence.headline: BEL discloses ₹533 crore of new orders since mid-September
aerospace-defence.summary: Bharat Electronics has received orders worth about ₹533 crore since its 17 September disclosure of ₹648 crore. The orders cover communication equipment, avionics, cyber products, unmanned aerial systems, electronic jammers, software, upgrades, spares and services.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: Steady flow of smaller orders between large platform awards supports order-book visibility for defence electronics, a key input to the sector's valuation.

aerospace-defence.headline: Army inducts 450 Nagastra-1R loitering munitions from Solar Defence
aerospace-defence.summary: Solar Defence and Aerospace has supplied 450 Nagastra-1R loitering munitions to the Indian Army, its largest single-batch delivery, under emergency procurement after trials in which it was the only one of four bidders to meet all parameters. The system has more than 80% indigenous content and a stated accuracy of 2 metres CEP. The contract value was not disclosed.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: Emergency procurement is accelerating scale orders for private-sector drone and munitions makers, strengthening the case for capacity investment and capital raising in the segment.

aerospace-defence.headline: Boeing delivers 161 commercial jets in Q3, 475 so far in 2026
aerospace-defence.summary: Boeing delivered 161 commercial aircraft in Q3 2026, including 124 737s and 22 787s, bringing year-to-date deliveries to 475. Its defence, space and security unit delivered 33 units in the quarter and 98 year to date.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: A steadier 737 cadence supports the aero-structures and component supply chain, including Indian build-to-print suppliers, as both OEMs head into a heavy Q4.

regulatory.headline: MoRTH draft sets BS-VII emission norms for cars and SUVs from April 2029
regulatory.summary: A draft notification dated 12 October applies BS-VII to M1 passenger vehicles from 1 April 2029, in phases running to 2035. Tailpipe limits stay at BS-VI levels, but the draft adds brake particulate limits from April 2031 (3 mg/km for pure EVs, 7 mg/km for others), a real-driving conformity factor of 1.0 from April 2030 and tighter onboard monitoring. Carmakers would prefer a 2032 start; commercial-vehicle rules are expected separately.
regulatory.whyItMatters: Compliance spend on testing, software and engineering competes with EV programmes for capital, and may reshape product timelines and supplier opportunities in emissions and braking technology.

regulatory.headline: WPI inflation climbs to a series-high 11.39% in September
regulatory.summary: Wholesale inflation rose to 11.39% from 9.92% in August. Fuel and power inflation reached 25.85% and manufactured products 9.76%, also a series high, while food articles rose to a 21-month high of 8.14%.
regulatory.whyItMatters: Broad input-cost inflation strengthens the case for the RBI's tightening stance and points to margin pressure for industrials and autos lacking pass-through clauses.
